verdict.rationale: Dynadot has no native automation or scheduled-workflow feature, so this is only partial. Its API (120+ actions, bulk adjustments, registering, renewing, DNS) lets users script their own background automations, but they must host and schedule them with external tools. A few built-in features also work unattended: aftermarket backorder requests, and the Watchlist, which monitors domains for expiry or status changes. The MCP server is conversational and assistant-driven rather than autonomous. Missing for 10: a native automation or workflow builder, scheduling or triggers, a documented autonomous agent or background-job capability, webhooks or event-driven actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
